Commentary of Ibn 'Atiyya (al-Muharrar al-Wajiz) on surah 85, verses 1–9:

(p-575) In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Tafsir of Surah al-Buruj

It is Meccan, by the consensus of the exegetes (mu'awwilin); there is no disagreement on this.

The Exalted and Majestic One said:

﴿By the sky containing the mansions of the stars,﴾ ﴿and the promised Day,﴾ ﴿and the witness and the witnessed.﴾ ﴿Destroyed were the people of the trench,﴾ ﴿the fire fed with fuel,﴾ ﴿when they sat over it,﴾ ﴿and they were witnesses to what they did to the believers.﴾ ﴿And they resented them for nothing except that they believed in Allah, the Almighty, the Praiseworthy,﴾ ﴿to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. And Allah is, over all things, Witness.﴾

People differed over "al-buruj." Al-Dahhak and Qatadah said: they are palaces. From this is the verse of al-Akhtal:

Like a Roman tower, built by a builder with plaster, baked brick and stones.

Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, said: al-buruj are the stars, because they display (tatabarraju) their light, and tabarruj means to show oneself and become apparent. The majority, and Ibn 'Abbas also, said: al-buruj are the stations (manazil) known to the Arabs, which are twelve according to how the Arabs divided them, and which the sun traverses in a year and the moon in twenty-eight days. Qatadah said: its meaning is "those possessing sand and water," meaning that they are built in the sky; and this is a weak opinion.

"The promised Day" is the Day of Resurrection by agreement; the Prophet (ﷺ) said so, and its meaning is "the Day that is promised."

(p-576) The words "mashhud" (witnessed) mean: upon it, or by it, or in it, and this follows from the disagreement over determining what is meant by ﴿witness and witnessed﴾. People differed over what is referred to by these two. Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, said: the witness is Allah the Exalted, and the witnessed is the Day of Resurrection. Ibn 'Abbas also, al-Hasan ibn 'Ali and 'Ikrimah said: the witness is Muhammad (ﷺ), and the witnessed is the Day of Resurrection. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, We sent you as a witness﴾ [al-Fath: 8], and He said of the Day of Resurrection: ﴿That is a Day whereon mankind will be gathered, and that is a Day witnessed﴾ [Hud: 103]. Mujahid and 'Ikrimah also said: the witness is Adam, peace be upon him, and all his offspring, and the witnessed is the Day of Resurrection. On this view, "witness" is a generic noun. Some who expounded the view of Mujahid and 'Ikrimah said: "witness" refers to a single man or a soul among souls, and in this there is a reminder of the insignificance of the wretched son of Adam; and the "witnessed" is the Day of Resurrection. Al-Hasan ibn Abi al-Hasan and Ibn 'Abbas also said: the witness is the Day of 'Arafah, and the Day of 'Arafah and the Day of Friday; and the witnessed is the Day of Resurrection. 'Ali, Ibn 'Abbas, Abu Hurayrah, al-Hasan, Ibn al-Musayyib and Qatadah said: "witness" is the Day of Resurrection, and "witnessed" is mankind. Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: the witness is you, O son of Adam, and the witnessed is Allah the Exalted. Ibn Jubayr said the reverse, and recited: (And sufficient is Allah as a witness). Abu Malik said: the witness is 'Isa, peace be upon him, and the witnessed is his community. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And I was a witness over them﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 117]. Ibn al-Musayyib said: "witness" is the Day of Tarwiyah, and "witnessed" is the Day of 'Arafah. Some people in the book of al-Naqqash said: the witness is Monday, and the witnessed is Friday; this was mentioned by al-Tha'labi. 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, said: the witness is the Day of 'Arafah, and the witnessed is the Day of Sacrifice (al-Nahr). He also said: "witness" is the Day of Resurrection, and "witnessed" is the Day of 'Arafah.

(p-577) Abu Hurayrah narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ): « "Witness" is the Day of Friday, and "witnessed" is the Day of 'Arafah. » This was said also by 'Ali, Abu Bakr and al-Hasan. Ibrahim al-Nakha'i said: the witness is the Day of Sacrifice (al-Adha), and the witnessed is the Day of 'Arafah.

The author, Qadi Abu Muhammad, may Allah have mercy on him, said:

He described these days as "witness" because they bear witness for those present in them concerning their deeds, and "witnessed" in what has passed of the sayings means "mushahad" with the letter ha' vowelled with fatha. al-Tirmidhi said: the witness is the guardian angels, and the witnessed are the people. 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Yahya, cited by al-Tha'labi, said: the witness is Muhammad, peace be upon him, and the witnessed are his community, like the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And We bring you as a witness against these people﴾ [al-Nisa: 41], meaning as a witness. It was also said: the witnesses are the prophets, peace be upon them, and the witnessed are their nations. al-Hasan ibn al-Fadl said: the witness is the community of Muhammad (ﷺ), and the witnessed are the people of Noah, peace be upon him, and the rest of the nations, according to the explicit hadith on this. Ibn Jubayr also said: the witness is the limbs that speak on the Day of Resurrection and testify against their owners, and the witnessed are their owners. Some scholars said: the witness is the angels who succeed one another among the community, and the witnessed is the Qur'an of Fajr, and its explanation is: ﴿Indeed, the recitation of Fajr is ever witnessed﴾ [al-Isra: 78]. Some scholars said: the witness is the star, and the witnessed upon which is the night and the day, meaning: the star bears witness to the coming of this and the going of that. From this is the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): « until the witness rises », "the witness" being the star. Some scholars said: the witness is Allah the Exalted, the angels and those possessed of knowledge, and the witnessed thing is His oneness and that the religion with Allah is Islam. It was also said: the witness is the creatures of Allah the Exalted, and the witnessed thing is His oneness. al-Tha'labi recited in this sense the verse of a poet:

And in everything there is a sign for Him, which indicates that He is the One.

(p-578) "Qutila" means: Allah did that to them because they deserved it; it is therefore in the form of a supplication according to human usage, not that Allah the Exalted supplicates against anyone. It was also said, on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas: it means "cursed"; and this is an interpretation by meaning. It was also said: it is a report that the fire killed them; this was said by al-Rabi' ibn Anas, and its explanation will come.

People differed over the People of the Trench (ashab al-ukhdud). It was said: they were a people who had a religion, and they had a king who committed adultery with his sister. Then some people urged him to establish in the people the marriage of sisters and daughters, so he compelled the people to this; many obeyed him, and a group disobeyed him. So he dug trenches (ukhadid) for them, which are long pits like moats, and kindled a fire for them and cast them into it. Then Magianism continued among his followers. 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, said: the Companion of the Trench was a king from Himyar, in the region of Mazari' in Yemen; he fought, he and the unbelievers, against the believers; then in the end he prevailed, and he burned them for their religion when they refused his religion. Among them was the woman with the child, who hesitated, and the child said to her: "Go into the fire, for you are upon the truth." al-Naqqash related from 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, that the prophet of the People of the Trench was an Abyssinian, and that the Abyssinians are the remnant of the People of the Trench. It was said: the People of the Trench are Dhu Nuwas, in the story of 'Abd Allah ibn al-Thamir which occurred in the biography (al-Sair). It was said: the People of the Trench were among the Children of Israel.

The author, Qadi Abu Muhammad, may Allah have mercy on him, said:

I have seen in some books that the Companion of the Trench is Muharriq, who burned a hundred men of the Banu Tamim. This view is objected to by the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿and they were witnesses to what they did to the believers﴾; and the objection is answered by saying that this statement is detached from the story of the People of the Trench, and that the intended meaning of His words "they" is the Quraysh, who used to torment the believing men and women.

People differed over the response to the oath. Some grammarians said: it is omitted, because the hearer knows it. Others said: it is His words "Qutila," and the implied sense is: "la-qutila" (indeed there was slain). Qatadah said: it is in His words: ﴿Indeed, the seizure of your Lord is severe﴾ [al-Buruj: 12]. Others said: it is in His words: ﴿Indeed, those who put the believers to trial﴾ [al-Buruj: 10].

His words "al-nari" (the fire) are an apposition (badal) to "al-ukhdud," and it is badal al-ishtimal (an apposition of inclusion). This is the reading of the majority, "al-nari" with a kasra on the ra'. A group read "al-naru" with a damma, meaning: the fire killed them. "Al-wuqud" with a damma is a verbal noun from "wuqidat al-nar" when it blazed, while "al-waqud" with a fatha on the waw is that which is fed to it. The majority read it with a fatha on the waw; al-Hasan, Abu Raja' and Abu Haywah read it with a damma.

The account of these people is that the unbelievers sat down, and the believers gathered, and it was proposed to them to enter into disbelief; whoever refused was thrown into the trench of the fire and burned. It is related that twenty thousand were burned. al-Rabi' ibn Anas, Ibn Ishaq and Abu al-'Aliyah said: Allah the Exalted sent a wind upon the believers which seized their souls, or something similar to this, and the fire came out and burned the unbelievers who were on the two edges of the trench. On this view, "Qutila" is the predicate of the two claims (khabara al-idda'). Qatadah said: ﴿when they sat over it﴾ means the believers.

"Naqamu" means: they transgressed. Most readers read "naqamu" with a fatha on the qaf; Abu Haywah and Ibn Abi 'Ablah read "naqimu" with a kasra on the qaf.

﴿By the sky containing the mansions of the stars,﴾ ﴿and the promised Day,﴾ ﴿and the witness and the witnessed.﴾ ﴿Destroyed were the people of the trench,﴾ ﴿the fire fed with fuel,﴾ ﴿when they sat over it,﴾ ﴿and they were witnesses to what they did to the believers.﴾ ﴿And they resented them for nothing except that they believed in Allah, the Almighty, the Praiseworthy,﴾ ﴿to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. And Allah is, over all things, Witness.﴾

People differed over "al-buruj." Al-Dahhak and Qatadah said: they are palaces. From this is the verse of al-Akhtal:

Like a Roman tower, built by a builder with plaster, baked brick and stones.

Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, said: al-buruj are the stars, because they display (tatabarraju) their light, and tabarruj means to show oneself and become apparent. The majority, and Ibn 'Abbas also, said: al-buruj are the stations (manazil) known to the Arabs, which are twelve according to how the Arabs divided them, and which the sun traverses in a year and the moon in twenty-eight days. Qatadah said: its meaning is "those possessing sand and water," meaning that they are built in the sky; and this is a weak opinion.

"The promised Day" is the Day of Resurrection by agreement; the Prophet (ﷺ) said so, and its meaning is "the Day that is promised."

(p-576) The words "mashhud" (witnessed) mean: upon it, or by it, or in it, and this follows from the disagreement over determining what is meant by ﴿witness and witnessed﴾. People differed over what is referred to by these two. Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, said: the witness is Allah the Exalted, and the witnessed is the Day of Resurrection. Ibn 'Abbas also, al-Hasan ibn 'Ali and 'Ikrimah said: the witness is Muhammad (ﷺ), and the witnessed is the Day of Resurrection. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, We sent you as a witness﴾ [al-Fath: 8], and He said of the Day of Resurrection: ﴿That is a Day whereon mankind will be gathered, and that is a Day witnessed﴾ [Hud: 103]. Mujahid and 'Ikrimah also said: the witness is Adam, peace be upon him, and all his offspring, and the witnessed is the Day of Resurrection. On this view, "witness" is a generic noun. Some who expounded the view of Mujahid and 'Ikrimah said: "witness" refers to a single man or a soul among souls, and in this there is a reminder of the insignificance of the wretched son of Adam; and the "witnessed" is the Day of Resurrection. Al-Hasan ibn Abi al-Hasan and Ibn 'Abbas also said: the witness is the Day of 'Arafah, and the Day of 'Arafah and the Day of Friday; and the witnessed is the Day of Resurrection. 'Ali, Ibn 'Abbas, Abu Hurayrah, al-Hasan, Ibn al-Musayyib and Qatadah said: "witness" is the Day of Resurrection, and "witnessed" is mankind. Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: the witness is you, O son of Adam, and the witnessed is Allah the Exalted. Ibn Jubayr said the reverse, and recited: (And sufficient is Allah as a witness). Abu Malik said: the witness is 'Isa, peace be upon him, and the witnessed is his community. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And I was a witness over them﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 117]. Ibn al-Musayyib said: "witness" is the Day of Tarwiyah, and "witnessed" is the Day of 'Arafah. Some people in the book of al-Naqqash said: the witness is Monday, and the witnessed is Friday; this was mentioned by al-Tha'labi. 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, said: the witness is the Day of 'Arafah, and the witnessed is the Day of Sacrifice (al-Nahr). He also said: "witness" is the Day of Resurrection, and "witnessed" is the Day of 'Arafah.

(p-577) Abu Hurayrah narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ): « "Witness" is the Day of Friday, and "witnessed" is the Day of 'Arafah. » This was said also by 'Ali, Abu Bakr and al-Hasan. Ibrahim al-Nakha'i said: the witness is the Day of Sacrifice (al-Adha), and the witnessed is the Day of 'Arafah.

The author, Qadi Abu Muhammad, may Allah have mercy on him, said:

He described these days as "witness" because they bear witness for those present in them concerning their deeds, and "witnessed" in what has passed of the sayings means "mushahad" with the letter ha' vowelled with fatha. al-Tirmidhi said: the witness is the guardian angels, and the witnessed are the people. 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Yahya, cited by al-Tha'labi, said: the witness is Muhammad, peace be upon him, and the witnessed are his community, like the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And We bring you as a witness against these people﴾ [al-Nisa: 41], meaning as a witness. It was also said: the witnesses are the prophets, peace be upon them, and the witnessed are their nations. al-Hasan ibn al-Fadl said: the witness is the community of Muhammad (ﷺ), and the witnessed are the people of Noah, peace be upon him, and the rest of the nations, according to the explicit hadith on this. Ibn Jubayr also said: the witness is the limbs that speak on the Day of Resurrection and testify against their owners, and the witnessed are their owners. Some scholars said: the witness is the angels who succeed one another among the community, and the witnessed is the Qur'an of Fajr, and its explanation is: ﴿Indeed, the recitation of Fajr is ever witnessed﴾ [al-Isra: 78]. Some scholars said: the witness is the star, and the witnessed upon which is the night and the day, meaning: the star bears witness to the coming of this and the going of that. From this is the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): « until the witness rises », "the witness" being the star. Some scholars said: the witness is Allah the Exalted, the angels and those possessed of knowledge, and the witnessed thing is His oneness and that the religion with Allah is Islam. It was also said: the witness is the creatures of Allah the Exalted, and the witnessed thing is His oneness. al-Tha'labi recited in this sense the verse of a poet:

And in everything there is a sign for Him, which indicates that He is the One.

(p-578) "Qutila" means: Allah did that to them because they deserved it; it is therefore in the form of a supplication according to human usage, not that Allah the Exalted supplicates against anyone. It was also said, on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas: it means "cursed"; and this is an interpretation by meaning. It was also said: it is a report that the fire killed them; this was said by al-Rabi' ibn Anas, and its explanation will come.

People differed over the People of the Trench (ashab al-ukhdud). It was said: they were a people who had a religion, and they had a king who committed adultery with his sister. Then some people urged him to establish in the people the marriage of sisters and daughters, so he compelled the people to this; many obeyed him, and a group disobeyed him. So he dug trenches (ukhadid) for them, which are long pits like moats, and kindled a fire for them and cast them into it. Then Magianism continued among his followers. 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, said: the Companion of the Trench was a king from Himyar, in the region of Mazari' in Yemen; he fought, he and the unbelievers, against the believers; then in the end he prevailed, and he burned them for their religion when they refused his religion. Among them was the woman with the child, who hesitated, and the child said to her: "Go into the fire, for you are upon the truth." al-Naqqash related from 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, that the prophet of the People of the Trench was an Abyssinian, and that the Abyssinians are the remnant of the People of the Trench. It was said: the People of the Trench are Dhu Nuwas, in the story of 'Abd Allah ibn al-Thamir which occurred in the biography (al-Sair). It was said: the People of the Trench were among the Children of Israel.

The author, Qadi Abu Muhammad, may Allah have mercy on him, said:

I have seen in some books that the Companion of the Trench is Muharriq, who burned a hundred men of the Banu Tamim. This view is objected to by the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿and they were witnesses to what they did to the believers﴾; and the objection is answered by saying that this statement is detached from the story of the People of the Trench, and that the intended meaning of His words "they" is the Quraysh, who used to torment the believing men and women.

People differed over the response to the oath. Some grammarians said: it is omitted, because the hearer knows it. Others said: it is His words "Qutila," and the implied sense is: "la-qutila" (indeed there was slain). Qatadah said: it is in His words: ﴿Indeed, the seizure of your Lord is severe﴾ [al-Buruj: 12]. Others said: it is in His words: ﴿Indeed, those who put the believers to trial﴾ [al-Buruj: 10].

His words "al-nari" (the fire) are an apposition (badal) to "al-ukhdud," and it is badal al-ishtimal (an apposition of inclusion). This is the reading of the majority, "al-nari" with a kasra on the ra'. A group read "al-naru" with a damma, meaning: the fire killed them. "Al-wuqud" with a damma is a verbal noun from "wuqidat al-nar" when it blazed, while "al-waqud" with a fatha on the waw is that which is fed to it. The majority read it with a fatha on the waw; al-Hasan, Abu Raja' and Abu Haywah read it with a damma.

The account of these people is that the unbelievers sat down, and the believers gathered, and it was proposed to them to enter into disbelief; whoever refused was thrown into the trench of the fire and burned. It is related that twenty thousand were burned. al-Rabi' ibn Anas, Ibn Ishaq and Abu al-'Aliyah said: Allah the Exalted sent a wind upon the believers which seized their souls, or something similar to this, and the fire came out and burned the unbelievers who were on the two edges of the trench. On this view, "Qutila" is the predicate of the two claims (khabara al-idda'). Qatadah said: ﴿when they sat over it﴾ means the believers.

"Naqamu" means: they transgressed. Most readers read "naqamu" with a fatha on the qaf; Abu Haywah and Ibn Abi 'Ablah read "naqimu" with a kasra on the qaf.

Commentary of Ibn 'Atiyya (al-Muharrar al-Wajiz) on surah 85, verses 10–16:

The words of the Exalted and Majestic:

﴿Indeed, those who persecuted the believing men and believing women and then did not repent, for them is the punishment of Hell, and for them is the punishment of the burning.﴾ ﴿Indeed, those who believed and did righteous deeds, for them are gardens beneath which rivers flow. That is the great triumph.﴾ ﴿Indeed, the seizure of your Lord is severe.﴾ ﴿It is He who originates and repeats.﴾ ﴿And He is the Forgiving, the Loving,﴾ ﴿Possessor of the Throne, the Glorious,﴾ ﴿Doer of what He intends.﴾

"Fatanu" (they persecuted) means they burned. One says "fatantu al-dhahab wa'l-fiddata fi'l-nar" (I subjected the gold and silver to fire), meaning I burned them. "Al-Fatin" is the black volcanic stones of the harra (lava field), because the sun seems to have burned them. Whoever says that these final verses concern the Quraysh takes "fitnah" to mean testing and torment. The statement of the Exalted, ﴿then they did not repent﴾, somewhat strengthens this interpretation, because this expression applies more firmly to the Quraysh than to those people who are known to have died in their disbelief. As for the Quraysh, among them at the time of the revelation of the verse were those who repented afterwards and believed in Muhammad (ﷺ). "Jahannam" and "al-Harīq" are two levels of the Fire. Whoever says that the Fire came out and burned the disbelievers who were sitting down makes "al-Harīq" refer to this world. "Al-Batsh" is seizing with strength and speed. "Wa yubdi'u wa yu'id" (He originates and repeats): al-Dahhak and Ibn Zayd said its meaning is that He "originates" creation by bringing it into existence and "repeats" it by the Resurrection. Ibn 'Abbas said, in substance, that this is general across all things, and it is an expression that He does everything, that is, He originates everything that is originated and repeats everything that is repeated. These two categories together cover all things. Al-Tabari said its meaning is: He originates the punishment and repeats it upon the disbelievers.

(p-580) "Al-Ghafur al-Wadud" are two attributes of action: the first is concealment over His servants, and the second is gentleness toward them and kindness to them. He specified the Throne by attributing Himself to it, as an honour and as an indication that it is the greatest of the created things. Hamza, al-Kisa'i, al-Mufaddal from 'Asim, al-Hasan, Ibn Wathhab, al-A'mash, and 'Amr ibn 'Ubayd read "al-majīdi" with a kasra on the dal, as an attribute of the Throne. This is based on the fact that majd (glory) and tamajjud may be attributed to many existing things, and they have said: "majadat al-dabbah" (the beast became fat) when it grew fat, and "amjadatha" when one treated it well. They have also said: "Fi kulli shajarin nar, wa-stamjada al-markh wa'l-'iffar" (In every tree there is fire, and the markh and 'iffar have become very fiery), meaning that their fire has increased. The rest of the readers and the majority read "al-majīdu" with a damma, as an attribute of God, the Exalted. The majority read "dhū al-'arsh" (Possessor of the Throne), while Ibn 'Amir transmitted "dhī al-'arsh" with a kasra, as an adjective to the words of the Exalted, ﴿Indeed, the seizure of your Lord﴾.

Commentary of Ibn 'Atiyya (al-Muharrar al-Wajiz) on surah 85, verse 17–22:

His statement, Mighty and Majestic is He:

﴿Has there come to you the story of the hosts,﴾ ﴿of Pharaoh and Thamud?﴾ ﴿Nay, those who disbelieve are in denial,﴾ ﴿and Allah encompasses them from behind them.﴾ ﴿Nay, it is a glorious Qur'an,﴾ ﴿in a preserved tablet.﴾

This is an address to the Prophet (ﷺ), meaning: set these disbelievers who oppose you behind your back and do not concern yourself, for Allah Most High has taken vengeance upon those mighty and fierce peoples, so how (much more) with these? And "al-junud" (the hosts): the gatherings prepared for battle and moving toward one single aim. "Pharaoh" stands in place of his people and his household, since he was their head. And "Pharaoh and Thamud" is in the genitive case as a substitution (badal) for "al-junud." Then He left the statement in its state and turned away from it to inform that these disbelievers against Muhammad (ﷺ) have no proof or evidence for them against him; rather, it is mere denial whose cause is envy. Then He threatened them with His statement: ﴿and Allah encompasses them from behind them﴾, that is, the punishment of Allah Most High and His vengeance. His statement ﴿from behind them﴾ means what comes after their disbelief and disobedience.

(p-581) Then Allah Most High turned away from their denial, nullifying it and refuting it, (saying) that it is a glorious Qur'an, that is, there is no blame in it. This is among what has preceded of describing other than Allah Most High with glory and magnificence. Ibn al-Sumayfa' al-Yamani recited "Qur'anu majidin" in the idafa (construct) form, and that Allah Most High is the Glorious (al-Majid). "Al-Lawh" is the Preserved Tablet in which are all things. The majority of readers recited "fi lawhin mahfuzin" with the genitive case, as an attribute of the tablet, which is known by this description. Nafi' alone—with a difference of transmission from him—and Ibn Muhaysin and al-A'raj recited "mahfuzun" with the nominative case as an attribute of the Qur'an, in the manner of His statement: ﴿And indeed We are its guardians﴾ [al-Hijr: 9], that is, it is preserved in hearts, not reached by error or alteration. Anas said: the Preserved Tablet is on the forehead of Israfil (peace be upon him). It was said: it is of a white pearl, related by Ibn 'Abbas. All of this is among what the chains of transmission fall short of establishing. Ibn al-Sumayfa' recited "fi luhin" with a damma on the lam.

The tafsir of Surah [al-Buruj] is complete, and all praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds.
